transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya, Marcus, Aisha, Tom

Auto-summary: we reviewed cost/unit metrics, caching and batching tradeoffs; some numbers look promising but need a follow-up throughput run with adjusted batching and KV cache warmup to validate tokens/$ at scale. Finance asked for explicit per-route costing.

[00:00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in, appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Priya Nair: hi, Priya here.
[00:00:08] Marcus Lee: Marcus, hi.
[00:00:09] Aisha Khan: Aisha on the line.
[00:00:11] Tom Rivers: Tom here.
[00:00:13] Ethan Cole: Ethan from Redwood, thanks.
[00:00:15] Sofia Martinez: cool, so agenda — tokens per dollar review, caching numbers, batching tradeoffs, then next steps. Ethan you want to start with the dashboard?
[00:00:25] Ethan Cole: yeah, I'll go through the runs. quick caveat — our labels in the telemetry are a bit messy, some of the run ids got renamed, so numbers are approximate. baseline run (no caching, baseline batch) gave about 0.72 tokens/sec per dollar on the m-48 setup. when we turned on prefix caching and KV cache hits at about 28% hit-rate we saw effective tokens/sec/$ jump to 1.3.
[00:00:56] Priya Nair: 28% hit-rate — is that realistic for our workload? our prompts are pretty templated but also have a lot of session history.
[00:01:05] Marcus Lee: yeah we ran a sampling over three days earlier this week; the hit-rate looked between 25 and 35 once we normalized for session lengths. I'll send the histogram.
[00:01:16] Ethan Cole: perfect that's consistent. then we did an optimistic run with warmed KV and more aggressive prefix caching plus 1.2x batching and that yielded ~1.9 tokens/sec/$ but p95 latency increased by ~60ms.
[00:01:33] Aisha Khan: can you translate tokens/sec/$ into our expected monthly bill? high level — at 1.9 tokens/$, with our projected 4 billion tokens per month what does that look like?
[00:01:44] Sofia Martinez: quick math — 4B tokens divided by 1.9 tokens-per-dollar is roughly $2.1M a month, raw inference cost. that excludes infra overhead, storage, and monitoring. we put a detailed sheet in the pilot folder.
[00:01:59] Tom Rivers: that number is high — what's the hosted vs dedicated break here? any discounts for reserved?
[00:02:08] Ethan Cole: good question. the Dedicated/reserved capacity with committed nodes reduces per-token costs by roughly 20-30% in our estimate depending on config. so that $2.1M could drop to about $1.5-1.7M with reserved capacity and slightly different batching. but there are tradeoffs — autoscaling flexibility and burst capacity differ.
[00:02:28] Priya Nair: does that 1.9 include quantization? we saw some notes about 4-bit runs.
[00:02:35] Ethan Cole: the 1.9 run was FP16 with KV/prefix caching; we also ran a 4-bit quantized run which got to 2.4 tokens/$ but we logged a small uptick in generation hallucination rates on a couple of tests — not a full eval but noticeable on some conversational prompts.
[00:02:52] Marcus Lee: what's the quality delta you saw? is it acceptable?
[00:02:56] Ethan Cole: from our quick eval: ROUGE-style and some task-specific metrics showed a 1-2% hit in the top-1 accuracy for Q&A style prompts; for ranking/embedding use-cases quantization had minimal impact. we'd recommend doing a focused quality check with your golden prompts if you consider 4-bit.
[00:03:12] Aisha Khan: finance question — how deterministic are these savings? I mean, caching hit-rate could vary a lot. we need a range for forecasting.
[00:03:21] Sofia Martinez: totally. that's why Ethan's follow-up run is important — we need to validate at scale with your actual traffic percentiles. Marcus, if you can give p50/p90/p99 and session distribution, we'll project optimistic/median/conservative savings.
[00:03:33] Marcus Lee: yes I'll pull that and share.
[00:03:36] Ethan Cole: also note the difference between prefix cache and KV cache — sometimes in notes people call it KV cash — we saw those transcriptions in the export — but prefix cache reduces repeated prefix tokenization while KV cache avoids recomputing KV cache across tokens for long conversations; combined they compound.
[00:03:55] Priya Nair: what was the warmup cost for KV? do we pay extra tokens to populate the cache?
[00:04:01] Ethan Cole: warmup cost is effectively extra tokens on first occurrences; in our run warmup added about 8-10% token overhead for sessions with long histories. but over multi-turn chats it amortizes and ROI is positive after about 3-4 turns depending on prompt length.
[00:04:18] Tom Rivers: latency is a concern — the team has strict p95 SLOs. how much does batching to improve tokens/$ push latency?
[00:04:25] Ethan Cole: higher batching increases throughput and tokens/$ but adds queueing latency. in our experiments moving from batch size baseline to 1.5x batch reduced cost-per-token by ~18% but increased p95 by ~70-90ms on these configs. for most of your synchronous chat flows p95 SLOs of 400ms would still be achievable, but we should map by route.
[00:04:45] Priya Nair: ok we have routes that are asynchronous (lower latency requirements) and some synchronous. can we route latency-sensitive traffic to lower-batch, reserved nodes and async traffic to high-batch pools?
[00:04:56] Ethan Cole: yes — Redwood routing supports policy-based routing by route/label. you can set low-latency pools for those routes and high-throughput pools for others; fallback policies can route to smaller models if needed.
[00:05:11] Marcus Lee: curious about cold-starts in private deployment — we may be considering VPC/on-prem in phase 2. do cold starts hurt caching assumptions?
[00:05:19] Sofia Martinez: they can, if cache isn't warmed. Private deployment gives you more control over locality — but you'd still want a small warm pool to keep caches hot. we can design auto-warm policies.
[00:05:28] Aisha Khan: finance again — aside from tokens, what about matrix of observability costs, egress, audit logs — would that be a large fraction?
[00:05:36] Ethan Cole: audit/observability storage and egress are secondary but not negligible — maybe 5-10% on top in our pilots depending on retention. if you need long retention for logs that can be more.
[00:05:45] Priya Nair: any security blockers? SSO/SAML and SOC2 were mentioned.
[00:05:50] Sofia Martinez: Redwood supports SAML, SCIM, SOC2 compliance, we can send the security pack — it'll be the standard docs we shared earlier. no blocker from a pilot perspective.
[00:05:58] Tom Rivers: good. back to numbers — can you put optimistic/median/conservative tokens/$ in the sheet so finance can run scenarios?
[00:06:05] Sofia Martinez: yes we'll add a three-scenario tab. the conservative case will assume 20% cache hit, minimal batching, no quantization; median is the runs we saw today; optimistic is warmed KV + 35% hit + 4-bit where quality ok.
[00:06:20] Ethan Cole: one more thing we noticed — repeated system prompts and tool calls in your flows gave outsized caching wins. if you can structurally move static context into system level we see up to 40% extra savings.
[00:06:33] Marcus Lee: we do have lots of repeated system text. we'll look into moving more to system-level.
[00:06:38] Priya Nair: about the follow-up run — Ethan, what exact config do you need from us?
[00:06:42] Ethan Cole: ideally: real traffic replay for ~60 minutes at peak, with KV/prefix caching enabled, batch multiplier 1.5 and 2.0 runs, include prefix hit-rates, KV hit-rates, p50/p90/p95 latencies and token counts — and please give us a warmed-run vs cold-run distinction.
[00:07:00] Sofia Martinez: we'll also include a quantized 4-bit run but mark it exploratory.
[00:07:05] Aisha Khan: timeline? finance needs the scenario sheet by Thursday.
[00:07:09] Sofia Martinez: we can have the updated cost model by 2025-06-19. Ethan will try to run throughput tests by 2025-06-20 and send logs.
[00:07:18] Tom Rivers: schedule the exec demo please.
[00:07:21] Sofia Martinez: noted. we'll send invite for 6/25.
[00:07:24] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[00:07:27] Priya Nair: small question — did you compare to Anthropic's pricing in the model?
[00:07:31] Ethan Cole: we included a comparison in the deck; on some workloads Anthropic similar models are within 10-20% of our hosted costs but differences in latency and hosting flexibility make the decision workload-dependent.
[00:07:43] Marcus Lee: ok thanks, that helps.
[00:07:47] Sofia Martinez: recap of next steps: Ethan run the two throughput runs and share logs; Marcus send traffic percentiles; Sofia share updated cost spreadsheet; schedule exec demo.
[00:07:58] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone.
[00:08:01] Tom Rivers: thanks all.

Notes: transcription sometimes spells 'KV cache' as 'KV cash' or 'Redwood Dedicate' in the auto-export. Attachments referenced: "pilot-cost-model-v2.xlsx" (in shared drive), "throughput-run-2025-06-16.log"
